title: Adding a cafe, drinks or public events to a glass studio: health permits, meals tax, ABC licenses, temporary food permits and city special events
question: My Staunton glass studio wants a small cafe, sip-and-blow evenings with wine or beer, and outdoor demonstrations at events. Which health, tax, alcohol and event approvals do I need?
office: Virginia Department of Health, Central Shenandoah Health District, Staunton-Augusta Environmental Health (food establishment and temporary food permits); Commissioner of the Revenue (meals tax); Virginia Alcoholic Beverage Control Authority (alcohol licenses); City of Staunton Parks & Recreation and Public Works (special events and street closures); Fire Marshal's Office (tents, open flame, cooking at events)
summary: Selling prepared food or drinks turns part of the studio into a restaurant under Virginia law. Before opening a cafe: send the Health District a Foodservice Plan Review Application ($40) with the menu, layout, equipment and finishes, then a Foodservice Permit Application ($40) at least 30 days before opening; the office at 1426 N. Augusta St. inspects before issuing and at least once a year after. Register with the Commissioner of the Revenue, add the 7% city meals tax to every taxable sale and file the monthly return by the 20th (3% discount for filing on time; the health permit goes with the business license application). To pour wine or beer at a cafe, apply to Virginia ABC for a retail on- and off-premises wine and beer license ($450 a year to the state plus up to $150 local tax; 60 to 90 days; a mixed beverage restaurant license needs a food-to-beverage ratio and costs $1,050 and up); ABC will not let you serve until the health permit issues, and you must tell the Commissioner when the ABC license comes. Without a cafe, occasional sip-and-blow nights can run on a banquet license ($40 per day, or an annual banquet license for a nonprofit) and free pours at a community art walk on an annual arts venue event license ($300, up to 12 days a year); the food side of such nights still needs a permanent or temporary food permit if food is prepared or served. Food or drink at an outdoor event needs a Temporary Food Establishment permit ($40, at least ten calendar days ahead, inspected before it issues). An event on city streets, parking lots or parks needs the city's Special Event Application at least 60 days ahead (insurance, vendors' business licenses, a liquor liability endorsement if alcohol is served), a street closure request through Public Works, Fire Marshal review of tents over 400 square feet and cooking, and a Public Activity Permit from the Police Department where City Code § 9.05.130 requires one.

steps.step: Decide the food and drink model: no food, packaged goods only, a cafe, or events only
steps.how: Selling only packaged or canned goods (bottled drinks, wrapped snacks) is exempt from the state restaurant license; preparing or serving food, pouring coffee or opening a bottle for a guest is a restaurant under Va. Code § 35.1-1 and needs the health permit, the meals tax and, for alcohol, an ABC license. A cafe gives you a permanent food permit that also covers the studio's own events (tell the Health District); events-only means a temporary food permit for each event and ABC banquet or arts venue licenses instead of a restaurant license. The alcohol choice also changes the ABC path: wine and beer with no spirits is simpler and cheaper than a mixed beverage restaurant license, which requires a food-to-beverage sales ratio.
steps.quote: Grocery stores, including the delicatessen portion that is a part of a grocery store selling exclusively for off-premises consumption, and places manufacturing or selling packaged or canned goods;

steps.step: Cafe: submit the Foodservice Plan Review Application ($40) to the Staunton-Augusta environmental health office
steps.who: Studio owner; Virginia Department of Health, Central Shenandoah Health District, Staunton-Augusta Environmental Health (1426 N. Augusta St., Staunton; 540-332-7830)
steps.how: The Health District requires plan review for any new food service establishment or a remodel. Send the Foodservice Plan Review Application (a 21-page packet, English and Spanish) with the $40 fee; the state regulation lists what plans must show: intended menu, anticipated volume, proposed layout, mechanical schematics, construction materials and finish schedules, equipment types and models, and standard procedures. Do this alongside the building permit plans, because sinks, hand-washing, grease, ventilation and finishes come up in both reviews. A certified food protection manager is required for a food establishment unless an exemption applies.
steps.quote: You will need to complete and submit a Plan Review Application, along with a $40.00 application fee, and submit it to the local health department office.

steps.step: Cafe: submit the Foodservice Permit Application ($40) at least 30 days before opening and pass the pre-opening inspection
steps.how: Once the plan review is approved, send the Foodservice Permit Application with its $40 fee at least 30 days before opening (the VDH page names the form but does not link it; ask the office). The permit is in the owner's or lessee's name and is not transferable; a change of owner needs a new application. The environmental health specialist inspects before the permit issues and then at least once every 12 months. Post the permit.
steps.quote: Transferring ownership of a facility also requires submission of a completed application.

steps.step: Register for the meals tax, charge 7% and file monthly
steps.who: Studio owner; Commissioner of the Revenue (City Hall, 1st floor; 540-332-3829)
steps.how: Every business in the city selling meals or beverages must register with the Commissioner, collect the 7% meals tax on prepared food and drinks (on top of the 5.3% state sales tax) and file the Meals Tax Return with payment by the 20th of the following month; filing and paying on time earns a 3% seller's discount, late payment costs 5% plus 10% a year interest. The health permit must go with the business license application. State law keeps tips, factory-sealed alcohol sold to take away and grocery food out of the tax. Full detail in meals_tax_filing.
steps.deadline: Return and payment by the 20th of the month following the tax month
steps.quote: To avoid penalty and/or interest, this return with payment must be filed on or before the 20th day of the month following the tax month.

steps.step: Cafe with drinks: apply to Virginia ABC for a retail license
steps.who: Studio owner; Virginia ABC (regional office listed by the city at 464 Commerce Square, Staunton; licensing 804.213.4400); Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: A retail on- and off-premises wine and beer license lets a restaurant sell wine and beer for drinking on the premises, with or without meals, and in closed containers to take away; the state fee is $450 a year and the local license tax for a restaurant in a city is up to $150. A mixed beverage restaurant license (spirits) costs $1,050 a year for up to 100 seats plus up to $200 locally and is granted only to a restaurant meeting the ABC food-to-beverage ratio. ABC says the application takes 15 to 30 minutes and processing averages 60 to 90 days; the application needs the health permit or proof it is pending, and ABC may issue on a pending application but you may not sell or serve until the health permit issues. ABC publishes notice and objections can be filed. Tell the Commissioner of the Revenue when the license issues so the local ABC license tax is added to the business license.
steps.deadline: Apply 60 to 90 days before you plan to serve
steps.fee: Wine and beer on- and off-premises $450 state plus up to $150 local; mixed beverage restaurant (up to 100 seats) $1,050 state plus up to $200 local
steps.quote: A retail on- and off-premises wine and beer license authorizes the licensee to sell beer and wine for on-premises consumption and to sell wine and beer in closed containers for off-premises consumption.

steps.step: No cafe but sip-and-blow nights: banquet licenses, or an annual arts venue event license for art walks
steps.who: Studio owner (or a nonprofit partner); Virginia ABC
steps.how: A banquet license lets the person in charge of a private banquet, or a nonprofit in charge of a special event, sell or give wine and beer in ABC-approved rooms for drinking there; a separate license is needed for each day ($40 per license, with exceptions under § 4.1-215), and the application can name an alternative location for an outdoor event. A nonprofit fraternal, patriotic or charitable organization can hold an annual banquet license for up to 12 banquets a year ($300). An annual arts venue event license ($300) lets an arts venue taking part in a public community art walk serve, but not sell, lawfully acquired wine or beer to adult patrons on its premises, limited to two 5-ounce glasses of wine or two 12-ounce beers per patron and 12 calendar days a year. ABC's Licensing Wizard walks through banquet licensing. If food is prepared or served at these nights and you have no permanent food permit, a temporary food establishment permit is needed too.
steps.deadline: Banquet licenses are per day; apply ahead of each event
steps.fee: Banquet license $40 per license; annual banquet license $300; annual arts venue event license $300
steps.quote: Except as provided in § 4.1-215 , a separate license shall be required for each day of each banquet or special event.

steps.step: Outdoor demonstrations or sales at events: Temporary Food Establishment permit for any food or drink served
steps.who: Studio owner or vendor; Staunton-Augusta Environmental Health
steps.how: Food or open-container drinks prepared or served at a fair, festival or market need a Temporary Food Establishment permit from the local health department: application and $40 fee at least ten calendar days before the event (the fee is waived once a year if you already paid a TFE fee in the calendar year elsewhere in Virginia, and for exempt churches and volunteer groups), listing every food item, where it is prepared, how it is transported and held, and the on-site person in charge, who must be a certified food protection manager unless exempt. A pre-operational inspection comes before the permit; the permit covers one event of up to 14 consecutive days and is not transferable. A studio holding a permanent food permit need not get a TFE permit if the food is prepared as its approved plans allow, but must tell the Health District.
steps.deadline: At least ten calendar days before the event
steps.fee: $40.00 per application (waived for a later event in the same calendar year if a TFE fee was already paid in Virginia)
steps.quote: A Temporary Food Establishment (TFE) is a type of food establishment that operates for a period of no more than 14 consecutive days in conjunction with a single event or celebration

steps.step: Events on city streets, parking lots or parks: Special Event Application 60 days ahead
steps.who: Event organizer; Parks & Recreation (events in city parks, 540.332.3945; other events 540.332.3812); Public Works (street closures and parking lots, 540.332.3892); Police Department (Public Activity Permit); Fire Marshal's Office
steps.how: Every event on city property, one-time or recurring, needs the Special Event Application (online form or PDF) at least 60 days ahead; the city may call a planning meeting and may deny late or unsafe applications, and you may not promote the event or commit to vendors until it is approved. The application asks about traffic, food and merchandise sales, alcohol and security, and requests resources: street closures or parking lot use (complete Section 1; Public Works reviews), electricity, fire and EMS support, fireworks or live fire demonstrations (Fire Marshal permit), food vendors (VDH and Fire Marshal inspection), park facilities, amusement devices and platforms over 120 square feet (building permit). Insurance: a certificate with $1,000,000 liability, the city named as additional insured, and a liquor liability endorsement if alcohol is served. All vendors need a city business license and collect their own taxes; a promoter's license may apply. Alcohol needs an ABC license and is allowed in parks only in specified locations by administrative policy; cooking is not allowed under tents, tents over 400 square feet need Fire Marshal inspection and over 900 square feet a building permit; a 20-foot fire lane must be kept; events near the Wharf lot on Saturdays are coordinated with the Farmers' Market. Noise is subject to the Noise Control Ordinance (§ 8.25.010) and a Police Public Activity Permit may be required under § 9.05.130.
steps.deadline: At least 60 days before the event
steps.fee: Not stated on the page read (the application has a fee-collected box); park facility fees apply where a park is used
steps.quote: Applicants may not promote a proposed event nor enter commitments for goods and services until receipt of approval of the event.

steps.step: Temporary street closure for a block party or loading
steps.who: Event organizer or studio; Public Works, Engineering Division (540.332.3858) and Public Works (540.332.3892)
steps.how: A street closure for an event goes in Section 1 of the Special Event Application and is reviewed by Public Works; the Engineering Division also publishes a Temporary Street Closure Request form (linked on its page and the city's permits list; the PDF has no archive copy and was not read). The applicant must notify affected businesses and residences as soon as possible.
steps.deadline: With the special event application (60 days) or as the form requires
steps.quote: If the event involves City street closure or use of a City parking lot, complete and attach Section 1.

steps.step: Open flame, cooking and tents at studio events: Fire Marshal
steps.how: Open flames in an assembly or dining area of a restaurant or drinking establishment are a permit item under the state fire code, and a live glassblowing demonstration at a public event is the kind of activity the Fire Marshal's Fire Prevention Activity Application exists for. Cooking is not allowed under a tent or canopy and open fires only in approved cooking appliances; tents of 400 to 900 square feet need a $25 Fire Marshal permit and larger tents a $100 building permit. Food vendors at city events are inspected by both VDH and the Fire Marshal. Detail in glass_studio_fire_permits.
steps.fee: Tent permit $25.00 per event (400 to 900 square feet); flame effects material indoors $100.00 per event (City Code § 15.25.055, read on eCode360)

caveats: City pages and PDFs are Internet Archive copies (dates in sources); VDH, ABC and law.lis pages were read live on 2026-10-19.

ABC: the fees quoted are the statutory state license taxes in § 4.1-231.1 and the local caps in § 4.1-233.1; ABC's application fees, the food-to-beverage ratio regulation, the required documents list and the application PDFs were not read. The VDH food-services page the city's instructions link returned 404 earlier; the Central Shenandoah page is cited instead.

Whether a glass studio that is not a restaurant can hold ABC banquet licenses for its own ticketed sip-and-blow nights (a banquet license is for the person in charge of a private banquet or a nonprofit's special event) is an ABC question; the arts venue event license covers free pours during a community art walk only.
Staunton's meals tax ordinance (ch. 3.40) was not read; the rate, due date, discount and penalties come from the city's return and pages (see meals_tax_filing).

The Temporary Food Establishment application cited is the statewide VDH form hosted on another district's site; the Staunton-Augusta office may supply its own copy. District pages elsewhere give different lead times (10 business days, 30 days); the VDH statewide page and form say ten calendar days.

The Special Events page and application name city staff for events in parks and elsewhere; only the office lines are recorded. The Public Activity Permit ordinance (§ 9.05.130) and noise ordinance (§ 8.25.010) were not read.
Which permits apply to a hot-glass demonstration at a city event (open flame, hot work, LP-gas) is for the Fire Marshal to say; see glass_studio_fire_permits.
